To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a programmable analog cochlear-implants processor has been developed in a standard 1.5 /spl mu/m Bi-CMOS technology with a low power consumption, high dynamic range, and robustness against power-supply and RF-noise variations.
a 211 /spl micro/W programmable analog cochlear-implants (cochlear-implant) processor has been designed and fabricated in a 1- /spl mu/m Bi CMOS process and tested in the laboratory.
a programmable analog processor has been designed and fabricated in a 1-1.5-/sup mu/m BiCMO S technology with a power dissipation of 211 /sup mu/W and a dynamic range of 77 dB.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a low-power, programmable analog cochlear-implants processor.
the development of an ultra-low-power programmably configurable analog bionic ear chip that can be used as the front end for cochlear-implants or portable speech recognition systems.
the design of ultra-low-power analog processors that are suitable for use in portable and implantable medical devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is a very significant achievement.
this work is the first to present a fully integrated programmable bionic ear processor with a 100-microW microphone and a power consumption of just 211 microW.
this is the most power efficient cochlear implant system ever developed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a low-power programmable analog processor for cochlear implant systems and that we are now in the process of developing a fully implantable system based on this processor.
we have developed an ultra-low-power programmably configurable analog bionic-ear processor that is capable of operating on a 100 mAh rechargeable battery for decades.

this processor is the first programmable analog cochlear-implants processor that has been demonstrated to operate with a power consumption that would be suitable for use in an implantable system with a 100-mA rechargeable battery.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the power consumption of the analog processor is dominated by the power consumption of an external electret microphone and that the analog front end of the processor is the most power-hungry block in the processor.
it is possible to build ultra-low-power analog signal-processing chips in standard CMOS processes.
the power consumption of the analog processor is dominated by its power consumption in idle (standby) mode.
